levelNote: Intermediate UGC NET questions testing literary context, interpretation, narrative techniques, satire and eighteenth-century drama.

questions.question: In Restoration comedy, what is most often exposed through witty exchanges and romantic intrigue?
options: The moral lessons of saints’ lives
The political economy of colonial plantations
The pretensions and hypocrisy of fashionable society
The necessity of classical unities in epic
questions.explanation: The comedy of manners tests social performance and exposes fashionable affectation.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which combination best characterizes the commercial Restoration theatre?
options: Actresses, indoor playhouses and movable scenery
Medieval pageant wagons and guild patronage
Boy actors exclusively, open-air amphitheatres and no scenery
Latin dialogue, liturgical ritual and church sponsorship
questions.explanation: After 1660 public professional theatre adopted actresses and spectacular indoor staging.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: In The Way of the World, which pair negotiates the famous proviso scene before marriage?
options: Dorimant and Harriet
Mirabell and Millamant
Almanzor and Almahide
Horner and Margery Pinchwife
questions.explanation: Mirabell and Millamant negotiate terms of married independence in Congreve’s proviso scene.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which play features Horner’s deception that he is impotent?
options: The Rover
The Country Wife
The Conscious Lovers
The Way of the World
questions.explanation: Wycherley’s The Country Wife uses Horner’s pretence of impotence as a central plot device.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What distinguishes the Restoration heroic play from a typical comedy of manners?
options: A humble village setting with rustic speakers
Elevated love-and-honour conflicts, often in rhymed couplets
A first-person sequence of private letters
Satire of urbane marriage negotiations only
questions.explanation: Heroic tragedy privileges grand passions, conflicts of honour and elevated verse.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: In Dryden’s Absalom and Achitophel, which figure corresponds most closely to Charles II?
options: Absalom
Zimri
King David
Achitophel
questions.explanation: The allegorical King David represents Charles II in the Exclusion Crisis satire.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Who is primarily satirized as Shadwell in Dryden’s Mac Flecknoe?
options: A betrayed Roman general
A loyal military commander
A heroic classical dramatist
The successor to a kingdom of dullness
questions.explanation: Shadwell inherits the throne of poetic stupidity from Flecknoe in this mock-heroic attack.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Why is All for Love formally distinct from Dryden’s earlier rhymed heroic drama?
options: It is a sequence of epistles
It is written chiefly in blank verse
It uses only ballad stanzas
It is entirely prose
questions.explanation: Dryden wrote All for Love in blank verse, reworking Antony and Cleopatra.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which critical issue is debated in An Essay of Dramatic Poesy?
options: The relative merits of ancient and modern, English and French drama
The proper number of letters in an English dictionary
The moral education of a servant heroine
The economic causes of enclosure
questions.explanation: Dryden stages a dialogue on classical and modern dramatists and French versus English practice.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: The Hind and the Panther (1687) is especially associated with which theme?
options: Rural depopulation after enclosure
Religious controversy and Dryden’s Catholic position
The history of a lock of hair
The domestic life of Crusoe on his island
questions.explanation: The allegorical animal poem explores religious debate after Dryden’s conversion to Catholicism.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which feature makes The Rape of the Lock a mock-epic?
options: It narrates an actual military conquest
It abandons all allusions to classical epic
It applies grand epic conventions to a trivial social quarrel
It treats only biblical creation
questions.explanation: The trivial cutting of Belinda’s hair is magnified by epic machinery and style.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which supernatural beings protect Belinda in The Rape of the Lock?
options: Valkyries
Furies
Sylphs
Muses
questions.explanation: Pope’s sylphs form the poem’s mock-epic supernatural machinery.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which principle is centrally explored in An Essay on Man?
options: The absolute autonomy of the individual from nature
Human limitations within a providentially ordered universe
The irrelevance of reason to moral life
The need to overthrow all poetic rules
questions.explanation: Pope examines humanity’s position and limits within the universal order.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Why does Pope enthrone Dulness in The Dunciad?
options: To satirize cultural decline and the triumph of bad writing
To narrate the plot of Pamela
To celebrate the return of medieval chivalry
To praise the heroic conduct of Marlborough
questions.explanation: Dulness personifies the spread of intellectual and literary mediocrity.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which statement best explains the “Augustan” quality of Pope’s heroic couplets?
options: They reject all metre and rhyme
They imitate Old English alliterative verse
They avoid ethical and social judgement
They seek balance, antithesis and controlled wit
questions.explanation: Pope’s couplets frequently balance clauses and sharpen satirical or moral arguments through antithesis.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the main satirical purpose of the Lilliput–Blefuscu conflict over egg-breaking?
options: To defend every policy of European courts
To celebrate the value of religious persecution
To expose the absurdity of sectarian and political disputes
To explain English maritime technology
questions.explanation: The quarrel exaggerates minor differences to reveal the irrationality of partisan conflict.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: How does Brobdingnag reverse Gulliver’s position in the first voyage?
options: He rules a kingdom of tiny people
He becomes a rational horse
He encounters only flying philosophers
He becomes tiny and vulnerable among giants
questions.explanation: Part II reverses the first voyage’s scale, undermining Gulliver’s sense of superiority.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the key effect of the calm, economic language in A Modest Proposal?
options: It presents a sentimental love narrative
It makes the proposed scheme sincere policy
It heightens horror through sustained irony
It removes the work’s political criticism
questions.explanation: A detached calculating voice exposes the cruelty of treating the poor as commodities.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What do the Yahoos chiefly represent in the fourth voyage of Gulliver’s Travels?
options: A court of Restoration comedians
Degraded aspects of human appetite and behaviour
A peaceful community of shepherd poets
The noblest achievements of scientific reason
questions.explanation: The Yahoos reflect a brutally pessimistic satirical portrait of human vice.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What did the fictional Spectator Club chiefly help Addison and Steele achieve?
options: A chronological history of Roman emperors
A social cross-section through which to observe contemporary manners
A continuous adventure story told by letters
A platform for anonymous court tragedies only
questions.explanation: The Club’s varied types allowed the essays to comment on different parts of social life.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which fictional gentleman became a recurring model of amiable rural conservatism in The Spectator?
options: Squire Allworthy
Parson Yorick
Sir Roger de Coverley
Isaac Bickerstaff
questions.explanation: Sir Roger de Coverley is the well-known country gentleman of the Spectator Club.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What purpose best describes Steele’s The Tatler?
options: To publish a complete dictionary in weekly parts
To revive medieval mystery plays
To serialize Tom Jones
To combine news, manners and moral commentary in short periodical essays
questions.explanation: Steele used The Tatler to blend social observation, criticism and ethical improvement.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Why were Addison’s Spectator essays influential in prose style?
options: They helped establish an accessible, polished conversational essay
They eliminated humour from moral writing
They promoted obscure technical vocabulary
They replaced prose with unrhymed pentameter
questions.explanation: Addison’s clear, urbane essays brought moral and literary criticism to a wide readership.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What narrative technique most helps Robinson Crusoe convey verisimilitude?
options: A detailed first-person account of practical everyday experience
A chorus that predicts every event
Continuous rhymed couplets describing gods
A series of anonymous newspaper editorials
questions.explanation: The realistic first-person narration details Crusoe’s labour, survival and decisions.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What does Crusoe’s construction of a self-sufficient island life especially foreground?
options: The impossibility of learning practical skills
The rejection of all religious reflection
Labour, property and individual resourcefulness
The rituals of the London theatre
questions.explanation: Crusoe’s survival emphasises work, ownership and providential self-examination.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What feature links Moll Flanders to the picaresque tradition?
options: The story follows Aristotle’s tragic unities
A resourceful protagonist moves through varied social worlds and adventures
The work uses only dialogue between allegorical animals
The heroine remains in one ideal pastoral village
questions.explanation: Moll’s episodic criminal and social experiences recall picaresque narration.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Why is A Journal of the Plague Year sometimes mistaken for direct eyewitness testimony?
options: Its vivid documentary-style narration creates a convincing historical voice
It contains an actual government medical register only
It narrates the events through supernatural sprites
It consists solely of sonnets written during the plague
questions.explanation: Defoe’s 1722 fictionalized account uses detailed reports and first-person observation to mimic testimony.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which social tension is central to Pamela?
options: An aristocrat’s desire to enter parliament
A servant’s resistance to her socially superior employer’s advances
A poet’s inability to complete an epic
A traveller’s encounter with rational horses
questions.explanation: Pamela frames a conflict of class, power and sexual coercion through letters.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What makes Clarissa especially significant within the epistolary novel?
options: Multiple correspondents offer competing perspectives on moral and psychological events
It is a single stage act without letters
The entire novel uses one external omniscient narrator
It is narrated by a chorus in heroic couplets
questions.explanation: Richardson’s multi-voiced letters expose motives, pressure and conflicting interpretations.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which quality of epistolary narration allows Richardson to present emotional immediacy?
options: Letters are written close to the events being described
All characters speak through a single allegorical mask
A narrator knows the future at every moment
A distant historian summarises events centuries later
questions.explanation: Richardson often presents feelings and decisions through letters composed as events unfold.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What did Fielding’s Shamela primarily challenge in Richardson’s Pamela?
options: Its description of giants in a foreign land
Its political attack on the Exclusion Crisis
Its use of theatrical scenery
The apparent sincerity and moral self-presentation of its heroine
questions.explanation: Fielding parodied what he saw as Pamela’s self-serving claims to virtue.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: How does Joseph Andrews initially relate to Richardson’s Pamela?
options: It translates Pamela into Latin
It continues Pamela as a historical epic
It reverses and parodies the servant-virtue situation with a male protagonist
It gives Pamela the role of an English queen
questions.explanation: Fielding initially satirizes Pamela by placing the virtuous servant in the position of a man.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What did Fielding call the kind of prose fiction developed in Joseph Andrews?
options: A heroic tragedy in blank verse
A comic epic-poem in prose
A metaphysical lyric sequence
A pastoral masque
questions.explanation: Fielding’s preface defines his narrative as a comic epic-poem in prose.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the narrative role of Squire Allworthy in Tom Jones?
options: A cynical manipulator from Clarissa
A French officer in A Sentimental Journey
A malicious lawyer plotting with Lovelace
A benevolent guardian whose judgment shapes Tom’s upbringing
questions.explanation: Allworthy raises Tom and becomes central to questions of charity and moral judgment.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which narrative technique distinguishes Tom Jones from Richardson’s epistolary fiction?
options: A sequence of rhymed dramatic monologues
A self-conscious, intrusive third-person narrator
A diary kept solely by Sophia Western
A novel made entirely of private letters
questions.explanation: Fielding’s narrator frequently addresses readers and comments on narrative technique.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Why does Tristram Shandy resist conventional chronological plotting?
options: It begins at the hero’s death and never moves backward
Its action obeys the three dramatic unities
It consists entirely of official legal documents
Its narrator repeatedly digresses before reaching the main events of his life
questions.explanation: The novel deliberately delays the life story through anecdotes, interruptions and digressions.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What is the function of the famous black page in Tristram Shandy?
options: It records a printing error corrected by the author
It visually marks mourning for Yorick
It lists the cast of a play
It represents the map of Lilliput
questions.explanation: Sterne experiments with typography by printing a black page to commemorate Yorick.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What does the word “sentimental” emphasize in Sterne’s A Sentimental Journey?
options: A strict chronological itinerary with no digressions
Sympathy and feeling in brief social encounters
The rules of epic battle
The necessity of impersonal scientific proof
questions.explanation: Yorick’s journey foregrounds emotion and sensibility rather than a comprehensive travel guide.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: How does Johnson’s Preface to Shakespeare respond to strict neoclassical rules?
options: It claims plays must never mix comic and serious material
It defends Shakespeare’s representation of general human nature despite broken unities
It rejects Shakespeare for violating all three unities
It argues that only Greek tragedy can be performed
questions.explanation: Johnson praises Shakespeare’s broad representation of life and questions rigid application of dramatic rules.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Why is Johnson’s Dictionary (1755) historically important?
options: It consists only of technical scientific terms
It was the first book ever printed in English
It removed all foreign-derived vocabulary
It systematically documents English words through definitions and literary quotations
questions.explanation: Johnson combined definitions with extensive illustrative quotations from English literature.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which philosophical problem drives Rasselas?
options: Whether women should perform on stage
Who should inherit the throne of Dulness
Whether lasting happiness can be found through different ways of life
How Crusoe learned to build a canoe
questions.explanation: Rasselas examines the human search for happiness and the limits of worldly choices.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which recurring concern unifies many of Johnson’s Rambler essays?
options: The geography of remote islands
A systematic attack on Shakespeare as a plagiarist
Moral self-examination and the uncertainties of human hopes
Court gossip presented as heroic romance
questions.explanation: The Rambler commonly examines ethical conduct, desire, disappointment and self-knowledge.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which statement best describes Johnson’s Lives of the Poets?
options: It is a satirical account of Lilliput
It is a novel told through love letters
It is a blank-verse epic of Adam and Eve
It combines literary biography with evaluative criticism
questions.explanation: Johnson joins biographical accounts with critical judgments on English poets.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Whose lives receive sympathetic attention in Gray’s Elegy?
options: The wealthy courtiers of Charles II alone
Only ancient Roman generals
The inhabitants of Lilliput
Obscure rural people whose talents remained unrealized
questions.explanation: Gray’s Elegy meditates on the forgotten dead and the unfulfilled potential of ordinary villagers.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What does the village graveyard symbolize in Gray’s Elegy?
options: The shared mortality of people across social ranks
The triumph of political satire
A kingdom in an epic allegory
A setting for fashionable courtship
questions.explanation: The humble graves prompt reflection on death, social inequality and remembrance.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which formal quality makes Gray’s Elegy recognizably different from Pope’s satirical couplets?
options: Unrhymed prose rather than verse
A dramatic dialogue between shepherds only
An epistolary narration told in letters
Meditative elegiac quatrains rather than pointed rhymed couplets
questions.explanation: The Elegy uses iambic-pentameter ABAB quatrains for reflective meditation.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Why does Kate Hardcastle pretend to be a barmaid in She Stoops to Conquer?
options: To escape with Tony Lumpkin
To disguise herself from Sir Roger de Coverley
To make the shy Marlow speak naturally to her
To steal the family fortune
questions.explanation: Marlow is awkward with respectable women but relaxed with those he thinks socially inferior.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which comic misunderstanding sets much of She Stoops to Conquer in motion?
options: Kate mistakes Marlow for a clergyman
Sir Charles mistakes Hastings for his son
Marlow mistakes the Hardcastle home for an inn
Tony mistakes London for Paris
questions.explanation: Tony misdirects the travellers, leading Marlow and Hastings to treat the Hardcastle house as an inn.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: Which family’s fortunes stand at the centre of The Vicar of Wakefield?
options: The Shandy family
The Primrose family
The Harlowe family
The Western family
questions.explanation: Dr Primrose and his household undergo reverses in Goldsmith’s novel.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ

questions.question: What social concern underlies The Deserted Village?
options: The decline of classical Greek dictionaries
Displacement of rural communities by wealth and changing landownership
The advantages of imperial warfare
The need for more court masques
questions.explanation: The poem laments depopulation and the destruction of village life in pursuit of wealth.
questions.src: user-supplied: AK Explained editorial practice MCQ
